EFW_Theo.name: Theo
EFW_Theo.role: Modern memory-bearer; ancient junior attaché to General Mero
EFW_Theo.visual: Young adult man with messy dark brown hair, pale-to-light skin, lean build, tired observant eyes, practical worn dark layers rather than a uniform. Present-day visual language is tactile and human: rumpled clothing, workwear, sketchbook/research materials, no heroic polish.

EFW_Rae.name: Rae
EFW_Rae.role: Modern memory-bearer; ancient strategic aide to Arbiter
EFW_Rae.visual: Young adult woman with dark asymmetric undercut hair, one side closely shaved and the longer side falling loose; light-to-medium skin with freckles, sharp expressive eyes, multiple ear piercings, visible geometric/linework tattoos on forearms, lean practical build, worn black or charcoal clothing. Her look is skeptical, investigative and grounded rather than glamorous.

EFW_Adrian.name: Adrian
EFW_Adrian.role: Neutral envoy, antiquarian and surviving memory of the war
EFW_Adrian.visual: Older adult man with shoulder-length silver-gray hair, weathered face, short gray beard/stubble, lean build, calm guarded eyes, dark worn contemporary clothing with understated quality. He should look like the same person in both eras, with age and bearing carrying continuity rather than costume spectacle.

EFW_Vark.name: Vark
EFW_Vark.visual: Older Black man, sturdy working build, deeply weathered face, short dark hair with some gray, practical excavation gear and battered helmet/headlamp. He reads immediately as a long-serving field foreman rather than security or military personnel.

EFW_Caelum.name: Caelum
EFW_Caelum.visual: Adult man with dark hair, trimmed beard/stubble, controlled formal appearance and pale structured Zenith institutional clothing. He should contrast Rae's worn dark practicality: ordered, clean, symmetrical, institutionally polished without looking villain-costumed.

EFW_Starbreaker.name: Starbreaker
EFW_Starbreaker.visual: Godlike Vanguard champion with pale blond hair, luminous white-and-gold fractured armor over a dark underlayer, radiant stellar geometry concentrated at the chest and around the body, and a weapon formed from compressed first-light energy. His silhouette is sharp, crystalline and ruptured rather than knightly or medieval. He is physically human and visibly exhausted beneath the cosmic scale.

EFW_Atlas.name: Atlas
EFW_Atlas.visual: Massive dark-skinned Vanguard champion with monumental physique, deep blue-black armor or layered battle garments traced by restrained gold gravity geometry. His design evokes mass, orbit and planetary weight rather than brute fantasy armor; small suspended spheres or orbital cues may appear when dramatically useful.

EFW_Flux.name: Flux
EFW_Flux.visual: Slender and androgynous-to-feminine Vanguard champion with dark hair, black-violet layered clothing/armor and a visual field of fractured probability: doubled edges, offset silhouettes, prismatic violet seams and spatial discontinuities. The body remains readable even when possibility effects multiply around it.

EFW_Afterlight.name: Afterlight
EFW_Afterlight.visual: Luminous pale-haired Vanguard champion whose design combines white, gold and living restoration motifs: seed-like geometry, translucent layers, delicate botanical structures and controlled radiance. She should feel regenerative and materially alive, not angelic or priestly.

EFW_Mero.name: General Mero
EFW_Mero.role: Human Vanguard general among cosmic champions
EFW_Mero.visual: Older human military strategist with gray hair and beard, scarred/weathered face, practical dark command armor or uniform, compact human-scale silhouette beside the champions. His design should communicate command experience without turning him into another godlike figure.

EFW_Oryon.name: Oryon
EFW_Oryon.visual: Lean, severe Concordant strategist in pale structured layers over dark formal underclothes, surrounded when useful by precise predictive diagrams, orbital lattices and cool geometric interfaces. His power language is foresight, systems and control—not sorcery.

EFW_Regent.name: Regent
EFW_Regent.visual: Older Concordant stabilizer with severe symmetrical black formal armor/robes, restrained gold boundary geometry and a circular stabilizing halo or field when power is active. His silhouette is architectural, balanced and immovable.

EFW_Arbiter.name: Arbiter
EFW_Arbiter.role: Concordant authority over civilization-scale triage and enforcement
EFW_Arbiter.visual: Imposing female Concordant authority in pale and dark judicial armor with sharp vertical crown-like structures integrated into the silhouette, severe geometric plating and restrained gold accents. Her presence evokes a living tribunal and irreversible judgment rather than royalty.

EFW_Redlin.name: Redlin
EFW_Redlin.role: Concordant battlefield commander and containment enforcer
EFW_Redlin.visual: Concordant battlefield commander built around containment: dark charcoal-to-black armor with deep red structural channels, circular/spherical joint and harness motifs, dense protective layers and a grounded battle-worn silhouette. Redlin should feel designed to absorb, restrain and hold rather than to radiate destructive power.

EFW_Kyn.name: Kyn
EFW_Kyn.visual: Distinctly non-Jesus-like Concordant empath with cool gray-blue skin, white/silver hair, elegant but unfamiliar facial geometry, white-teal-gold layered clothing and organic branching or neural motifs. Kyn's design communicates openness, sensory burden and connection without religious messiah imagery.

EFW_OlyriaTrench.name: Olyria-Prime Trench
EFW_OlyriaTrench.text: Working excavation cut into black bedrock on Olyria-Prime; heavy drills, work lamps, dust, ladders, shift gear and tired crews. Keep figures readable against the dark industrial environment with deliberate warm work-light separation, reflective surfaces and controlled atmospheric depth rather than uniform low-value murk.

EFW_ZenithArchives.name: Zenith Spire Archives
EFW_ZenithArchives.text: Institutional archive high in Zenith Spire; ordered shelves, old ledgers, current records, secure desks and long views over the planet. Use a brighter controlled architectural field behind characters so silhouettes separate clearly; Rae's dark practical styling should read immediately against ordered pale/cool institutional surfaces.

EFW_SectorFour.name: Sector Four Excavation
EFW_SectorFour.text: Newly opened excavation section where the Desert Marker emerges from black bedrock amid work platforms, dust and temporary lighting. The Marker is ancient, dark and deliberate; use focused work lights and reflected edge light so Theo, Vark and the object remain distinct instead of merging into one dark mass.

EFW_GridRuins.name: Stabilizing Grid Ruins
EFW_GridRuins.text: Damaged excavation tier after the first memory rupture, with broken platforms, dust, abandoned tools and stunned workers. Preserve the established Olyria palette but separate foreground figures from wreckage through directional practical light and atmospheric falloff.

EFW_TelemetryRoom.name: Zenith Telemetry Room
EFW_TelemetryRoom.text: Secure Zenith records room with controlled access, workstations, archive terminals and institutional oversight. Interfaces are functional evidence, not generic holographic decoration. Keep backgrounds cleaner and brighter than Rae's silhouette; preserve Caelum's lighter formal styling as a distinct second value family.

EFW_TriageTent.name: Olyria Triage Tent
EFW_TriageTent.text: Temporary field medical tent with cots, paper forms, ordinary supplies, tired workers and bad coffee. Human-scale, practical, comparatively brighter than the trench; let faces, bandaged hand, paper incident form and small acting beats read clearly without cinematic murk.

EFW_LowerArchives.name: Lower-Tier Archives
EFW_LowerArchives.text: Older archive stacks beneath the polished public levels, filled with physical books, sealed records and infrequently used storage rooms. Dimmer than the upper archive but not muddy: use localized pools of readable light, pale paper/stone/metal surfaces and depth separation around Rae and Adrian.

EFW_ObservationDeck.name: Zenith Observation Deck
EFW_ObservationDeck.text: High-altitude observation deck overlooking Zenith Spire and the planet below, with quiet public space and ordinary disposal infrastructure. Use the luminous exterior/city/planet view as controlled negative space so Rae and Caelum stand out cleanly in silhouette and facial value.

EFW_AbandonedTrench.name: Abandoned Trench
EFW_AbandonedTrench.text: Shut-down excavation cut with sparse work lights, scrap, deep shadow and enough loose material to conceal the reopened site. Dark environment, but preserve facial readability and the industrial cutter through selective practical light, rim separation and uncluttered staging.

EFW_CompactedEarth.name: Compacted Earth Above Sector Four
EFW_CompactedEarth.text: Surface above buried Sector Four beneath silent excavators and open stars, exposed and still after the work crews leave. Night scene with clear moon/star/industrial edge separation; Theo, Adrian and the small Marker fragment must remain readable without bathing the page in generic glow.

EFW_ZenithResidentialTransit.name: Zenith Residential and Transit District
EFW_ZenithResidentialTransit.text: Ordinary inhabited present-day residential rooms and public transit access below the institutional Spire: rain-dark windows, repaired furnishings, practical bags, personal objects, commuters and quiet late-night transport. Remain tactile, contemporary, and human-scale. Avoid futuristic spectacle, legible unscripted signage, magical effects or elegant hotel-like emptiness.

EFW_OlyriaPrime.name: Olyria-Prime
EFW_OlyriaPrime.text: Industrial excavation colony organized around deep field cuts, worker support spaces and survey infrastructure. Visual language: black bedrock, hard industrial geometry, workwear, amber-white practical lights, cool atmospheric distance and strong subject/background separation. Avoid uniform darkness, muddy brown grading or generic mining-world sepia.

EFW_ZenithSpire.name: Zenith Spire
EFW_ZenithSpire.text: Administrative and archival center where institutional authority is expressed through controlled access, sealed records and elevated public spaces. Visual language: ordered pale/cool architectural surfaces, disciplined geometry, restrained interfaces and luminous depth that clearly separates people from background. Avoid generic neon cyberpunk clutter or beige institutional filler.

EFW_VaelTor.name: Vael-Tor
EFW_VaelTor.text: Rainy civilian transit and port city whose current concourses, archives, apartments, utility corridors and landing infrastructure have accumulated directly over much older foundations. Present-day life should feel ordinary, busy and inhabited: wet glass, luggage, vendors, transit signage, maintenance work, balconies, service vehicles and mixed-age construction. Older stone and the buried black dreadnought surface appear as physical layers inside that everyday city, not as a separate fantasy ruin. When the forgotten war becomes visible, preserve residents and refugees as the scale reference; avoid turning Vael-Tor into a generic battle zone, neon megacity or pristine spaceport.

EFW_PaxAeterna.name: Pax-Aeterna
EFW_PaxAeterna.text: Treaty-city and evacuation hub built around severe civic stone architecture, broad public chambers and a black treaty table whose scale is human rather than ceremonial-fantasy. In the ancient timeline, open doors and galleries keep the civilian evacuation visible from political spaces: departure gates, crowded concourses, transport queues, luggage, medical carries and ordinary city streets sit immediately beside civilization-scale decisions. In the present, the treaty vault survives as a quiet ceremonial ruin inside ordinary civic life, with the same table, empty chair and worn architecture preserved after their meaning was forgotten. Keep the location inhabited and politically human; avoid throne-room grandeur, mystical temples, glowing control chambers or abstract war-room dashboards.
